Here are some of the important technology stories from this week:
Nvidia unveils massive $150B increase to share buyback program
Nvidia
said its board of directors has increased the size of its buyback program by

, using its massive balance sheet to buy back its stock. The $150B increase leaves Nvidia with $235B in buyback authorization. It is the largest buyback program in U.S. history, according to data compiled by Bloomberg.
AMD to acquire World Labs in $8.2B all-stock deal
Advanced Micro Devices
it would acquire World Labs, an AI model and research lab, in an all-stock transaction is valued at nearly $8.2 billion.

The surprise announcement was praised by analysts from Wall Street. Citi analyst Atif Malik said the decision to add World Labs and its founder, Fei-Fei Li (widely referred to as the “godmother of AI”), gives the company “deeper visibility” into how AI models are evolving.

RBC analyst Srini Pajjuri echoed those sentiments, suggesting that the deal to acquire the privately held AI research lab could "help position the company to offer full-stack solutions for robotics, simulation, and physical AI markets, which are in early stages."
Micron, Accenture quarterly results impressed investors
Micron Technology
demonstrated durability in its fourth-quarter
and outlook as its strategic customer agreements, or SCAs, continued to increase. As a result, analysts continue to see upside for the stock, which has already more than sextupled over the past year.
Similarly, investors were impressed after Accenture
reported fiscal quarterly results that exceeded expectations on both revenue and bookings. Shares closed nearly 16% on Thursday.
In other news,
HPE
closed nearly 4% higher on Wednesday after the company said it won a $1.2B order of AMD's
Helios AI rack from cloud infrastructure company Vultr. The company also increased its outlook for 2027, citing gains in networking.

The company now sees networking growth in fiscal 2027 in the high-teens to low-20s on a percentage basis as it is gaining share in the data center networking market. Data center networking revenue is expected to grow at a low-to-high 50s percent compound annual rate through fiscal 2029.
Anthropic
intends to launch its initial public offering before the Thanksgiving holiday begins, according to Bloomberg.
As per another Bloomberg News report,
Broadcom's
Wall Street syndicate is starting to gather $60B of fresh AI chip financing to benefit Anthropic PBC and other companies.
Meta Platforms
is adding an entirely new platform to target organizations, Meta Enterprise Platform, and the social media giant has tapped MongoDB

CEO Chirantan “CJ” Desai to lead the effort. The company also introduced Muse for Small Business, expanding its AI agent with new skills and app connections designed to help small businesses manage their operations.
